thread_analysis.thread_summary: Koizumi Lighting (contact Koji Kawasaki, later Mitsuhiro Yoshikubo, R&D Center) is a long-running repeat customer of Allion (Masaya Iida, Toshitaka Mochizuki, Itsuo Sakai, lab engineer Kenichi Ushiroebisu) for Bluetooth SIG certification of BLE-module-equipped lighting fixtures. The thread spans an earlier 2024 registration cycle (DIS profile + RF PHY testing for a lamp lineup, including account-access and derivative-registration questions) folded into a 2025 request (August-November) for a new module ('BM043,' Telink-based) registration, culminating in a multi-round RF PHY DTM 'LE Reset' non-response troubleshooting saga (with an AoA/AoD command-variant red herring along the way) that was ultimately traced to a defective/misconfigured module sample and resolved via manufacturer replacement, a profile-test ICS-declaration fix for an optional failing item, a self-corrected RF PHY frequency-parameter error, and finally a bulk derivative-registration request for roughly 150 additional product models.
all_questions_found: How to resolve a SIG account locked out due to an inaccessible former-employer email? (see thread_0013_case_01)

Can an antenna variant be registered as a derivative product, does the one-formal-plus-free-derivatives approach still apply for a 20-model lineup, and is SoftDevice S113 acceptable? (see thread_0013_case_02)
What test sample condition (prototype/nameplate/socket/app) is acceptable for DIS profile testing? (see thread_0013_case_03)
What registration evidence is needed for a new module (BM043) given two overlapping candidate reference QDIDs, and what was missing from the first quote? (see thread_0013_case_04)

Does exposing UART TX/RX leads disqualify an otherwise-unmodified profile test sample, what equipment and wiring connects a DUT to the InterLab test system, and what photo checklist confirms a sample is properly prepared before shipment? (see thread_0013_case_05)

Why does the RF PHY DTM test sample fail to respond to the 'LE Reset' command across multiple replacement samples (including an inconsistent-results detour involving AoA/AoD command variants), and how to phrase the question to the module manufacturer? (see thread_0013_case_06)
Can a failing optional DIS profile test item be resolved by changing its ICS declaration to 'Not Supported' instead of fixing firmware? (see thread_0013_case_07)

Which Mid/Low/High Frequency values apply for RF PHY testing given the product's declared Core Specification version and device role, and what happens when the test tooling no longer supports a legacy spec version's exact required values? (see thread_0013_case_08)
How to bulk-register approximately 150 additional product part numbers as free derivative models via the SIG-designated Excel import mechanism? (see thread_0013_case_09)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Repeated formal quotation requests, order confirmation, invoice/payment timing, and multiple internal logistics threads (sourcing a USB-UART converter, sample shipping/connector swaps, a test-plan-spreadsheet mix-up with an unrelated customer) -- routine project administration without a generalizable technical lesson.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread's most valuable technical content is the extended RF PHY DTM troubleshooting saga (case_06), now enriched with a genuine intermediate diagnostic detour: an AoA/AoD-specific command variant (v2/v3) caused inconsistent, order-dependent Success/ERROR results when issued to a SoC that didn't support it, illustrating that 'inconsistent across retries' and 'fails consistently at the first command' are different failure signatures pointing to different causes. Case_08 (found only in this redo pass) is a strong example of an expert self-correcting a device-role-dependent spec citation and disclosing a test-tooling limitation directly to the customer rather than papering over it. Case_07 demonstrates a cheap, no-retest resolution path (ICS declaration change) for a failing optional test item, while case_09 documents the SIG-designated bulk Excel import mechanism for large-scale derivative registration.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0013_case_01 through thread_0013_case_09 for case-specific decision logic; the throughline is distinguishing what genuinely disqualifies a sample/registration path or requires deeper investigation (module identity changes, true layer gaps in reference QDIDs, a consistent first-command DTM failure) from what does not or has a cheap fix (antenna implementation variety, convenience wiring, an optional failing test item, an unsupported AoA/AoD command variant causing inconsistent-not-consistent failures).
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; the highest-risk item remains case_06, where without isolating the failure to the serial/firmware layer (and without recognizing the AoA/AoD command-variant detour as a distinct, separately-resolvable inconsistency pattern), the customer could have spent significantly more time chasing the wrong root cause. Case_08 also carries real risk: an uncorrected device-role mix-up in a frequency-parameter citation would have left technically incorrect registration evidence in the final report.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The consultant's first answer on the RF PHY Mid Frequency question (case_08) cited the wrong device-role definition (Broadcaster/Observer instead of Peripheral) for the customer's declared Core Specification version, requiring a self-correction and report revision after directly rechecking the spec text -- a useful example of catching and transparently correcting an error rather than letting it stand uncorrected in the final report.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For a long-running repeat customer relationship spanning multiple registration cycles and new modules, maintain a structured, layer-by-layer diagnostic approach when a test sample fails early in a command sequence, and treat inconsistent/intermittent failures as a distinct diagnostic category from consistent first-command failures, since they often point to different causes (e.g., an unsupported command variant vs. a defective Test Application). When a spec-derived parameter depends on device role as well as version, verify against the exact spec text for the customer's actual role before answering, and proactively self-correct and disclose tooling limitations rather than letting an error or limitation pass unaddressed.
